assemblerItemCapsNote: HARD per-component item caps enforced by the assembler (_cap_tab_items in assembly/core.py). Deliberately INDEPENDENT of densityGates above: densityGates is advisory steering text shown to the planner LLM (what to aim for), these caps are the code backstop (what ships regardless of prompt drift) — e.g. step_player is steered to 10 but capped at 25. moment_track's cap additionally scales with video duration in code (evenly sampled, clamped 20-60).
domainRequirementsNote: Per-domain assembled-output validation (_validate_domain_requirements in assembly/core.py): `required` components are backfilled from defaultTabs when the planner drops them (promotion equivalents count, e.g. comparison_radar satisfies comparison); `max` caps per-component tab counts; `forbidden` components are stripped at plan post-validation (before extraction burns tokens) AND again at assembly as a backstop — a forbidden component is never rendered for that domain regardless of what the planner emits. quiz_arena is educational-only (learning/language/tech/science). Every domain must have an entry — an empty `required` is a deliberate decision (music: lyrics_karaoke optional so videos without per-line timing don't fail; podcast: moment_track segments are the spine; news: claims_tracker is the signature accountability surface; gaming: tier_list; sport: formation_diagram).
playbooksNote: Video-subtype layout playbooks keyed '<domain>:<format>' (format from the tier probe). Semantics: `forbidden` is a UNION with the domain's forbidden list; `required` OVERRIDES the domain's required list when present; `preferred` and `planGuidance` are rendered into the plan prompt's dynamic block so the LLM designs within the contract it will be held to. Enforcement lives in effective_requirements() (summarizer shared_config/domain_config.py) — consumed by plan post-validation and the assembly backstop.

gaming:unboxing.planGuidance: Box-opening / TCG pack-opening video: the pulls ARE the content. Rankings = the pulled cards (rarity or market-value bracket as tier, why it matters as reason). Highlights = the pull moments with timestamps. Never quiz the viewer on an unboxing.

review:unboxing.planGuidance: Product unboxing: lead with what was revealed and first impressions. Specs and contents as info_grid, reveal moments as moment_track. Never quiz the viewer on an unboxing.

visualCriticalityNote: Adaptive frame-pipeline effort (derive_tier in media/visual_tier.py). HIGH: the visuals are the content (unboxings, travel, food) — over-select candidates and vision-describe them all so subject-matter frames win over presenter shots. LOW: talky formats where frames are decoration — skip vision. Everything else STANDARD. Derived from the tier probe (domain, format, has_visual_demo — derive_tier(probe, title)) which runs at transcript-ready; the frames branch waits for it at most 3 s before Step 6b, then falls back to the metadata rule (category/title keywords). highFormats: a probe format that alone makes a video HIGH.

dataSourcesNote: Extraction field registry, one entry per path the planner may name as a tab dataSource (rendered into component_toolkit.txt's {valid_datasources} placeholder by render_valid_datasources() in the summarizer's shared_config/domain_config.py — entry order IS the prompt order). `field` is the key path inside the domain's extraction object (dotted for nested lists, e.g. tech.setup.commands). `kind`: list | object (an object counts as one item). `components`: components that can render the path (first = the defaultTab component when the path backs one). `siblings`: other paths sharing a component with this one, which can stand in when it is empty — assembly's sibling swap is component-based, so a sibling may differ in kind (fitness.exercises list ↔ fitness.timer object, both workout_room); every defaultTab sibling (sibling_datasources()) must be listed here. `requiresEvidence`: Appendix-C evidence key that must not be doubly-false for a tab on this path (null = never demoted). `waitsForVisual`: the field's content comes from the screen, so its extraction waits for frame annotations — gaming.highlights (on-screen pulls/plays) and the tech paths read off screen-shared code: tech.snippets, plus tech.patterns, tech.cheatSheet and tech.setup.commands, which quote the same on-screen code/terminal; transcript-driven paths (e.g. narrative.keyMoments) stay false. `cap`: max items asked for (largest SCALING bound in the domain schema, clamped to the primary component's assemblerItemCaps entry so extraction never asks for items the assembler truncates — e.g. language.phrases 25 (spot_explorer), language.vocabulary and podcast.quotes 15 (flash_deck); else the primary component's assemblerItemCaps/densityGates max; learning.timestamps = the assembler's duration-scaled moment_track max 60; music.lyrics = 200 because lyrics_karaoke is uncapped and the schema asks for all lyrics). `outputWeight`: observed output tokens per item (whole object for kind=object), measured 2026-10-07 over the 31 stored v8 docs in the DEV Mongo (20 unique videos; read-only): mean cl100k tokens of each stored item (json.dumps) × a calibration factor of 1.488 (median of ledger tokens_out ÷ cl100k tokens of the stored extraction, over the 26 docs with exactly one Haiku extraction call) for extraction paths, and o200k × 1.144 (gpt-4o-mini; median over the 13 single-call docs whose quiz/flashcards/scenarios were all kept) for enrichment.quiz. 31 paths are observed (≥ 3 items); the other 30 (domains absent from dev: project, review, language, science, podcast, news, narrative; plus fitness.timer, gaming.loadout, gaming.walkthrough) use the schema skeleton item's cl100k size × the observed-vs-skeleton median ratio (2.025, over the 30 observed extraction paths) × 1.488. Initial values, tuned later.
demoteToNote: Plan-time demotion ladder used by reconcile (pipeline-1min phase 3) when a tab's dataSource `requiresEvidence` key is false in BOTH the plan and the video memory: walk the list and take the first component the same dataSource lists in dataSources[*].components; an empty list means drop the tab. Independent of the assembly-time _DEMOTE_LADDER (assembly/promotion.py), which reacts to assembler failures after extraction. Entries beyond the brief's six mirror that ladder minus display_section, so every component of an evidence-gated dataSource has an entry.
requirementEvidenceNote: Evidence key gating each domain's `required` component: the component is backfilled (domainRequirements) only when this key is not false in both the plan and the video memory. Domain required components not listed here (language/science spot_explorer, podcast moment_track) stay unconditional.
quizEnrichmentNote: Quiz-only enrichment (pipeline-1min phase 1d): the quiz call runs only for these domains (the ones whose domainRequirements do not forbid quiz_arena); `flavor` is the per-domain role line of enrich_quiz.txt, carried over from the per-domain enrich prompts it replaced in phase 1d. The call is demand-driven: it runs only when the plan has a quiz_arena tab or a tab that can host a quick_quiz (needs_quiz() in the summarizer's services/pipeline/enrichment.py).

flavor.learning: Test understanding with specific details from the content (not trivia) — actionable knowledge the viewer can apply immediately.
flavor.language: Test comprehension of vocabulary, grammar rules, and usage — practical language skills the viewer can use immediately.
flavor.tech: Think like a senior developer onboarding a teammate — test understanding of technical decisions, code patterns, and commands from the video.
flavor.science: Test understanding of scientific concepts, facts, and relationships — and their real-world applications.

groupingNote: Phase-3 extraction grouping: at most maxTextGroups text groups (+ 1 visual group for waitsForVisual paths); a domain splits by field when Σ outputWeight × expected items exceeds groupOutputBudget output tokens.
